subject: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination - FinWise
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>, Chris Lee <chris@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs & next steps

Alex / Chris — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we can sync on the customer-led load test: 

Summary of agreed SLO goals (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms (non-streaming generation); p99 <= 900ms. For streaming responses, average chunk latency <= 200ms.
- Throughput: sustained target ~500 req/s (typical request ~1k tokens).
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions/streams during peak.
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx errors over the 2 hour test.

Load test plan (proposed):
- Test tool: customer-led k6 (we can also accept Locust)
- Ramp: 10m ramp to target sustained load, 90m steady-state, 20m cool-down
- Test window: proposed Thu 2027-07-01 22:00 - 00:00 UTC (2 hours). If that doesn't work for you, tell us preferred windows.
- Test accounts: we'll provide test API keys and a CSV of test users (see attachments).
- Allowlist: please provide source IPs so our infra team can allowlist.

Attachments: finwise_k6_script.js (example load profile), test_accounts.csv, redwood_load_test_plan.pdf

Next steps:
1) You confirm the SLO numbers above and the test window (or propose alternate).
2) Provide your test source IPs for allowlist.
3) We'll provision test API keys and share endpoints + a dedicated ingestion route for the test.

I'll loop in Marissa to share the k6 script and specifics on headers/auth. Happy to jump on a 15m sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Lee <chris@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks Logan — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications before we lock the window: 

- Test window: Thu 2027-07-01 is our local end-of-quarter close; could we move to Sat 2027-07-03 00:00 - 02:00 UTC instead? That would minimize risk for our production teams.
- Streaming semantics: for streaming tests, do you plan to test chunked responses (server push) or simulated short polling? We want streaming to reflect the same client behavior as production (clients open a stream and receive incremental chunks).
- IP allowlist: our outbound IPs (from our test runners) are 52.23.112.45 and 35.182.90.12. Please confirm your infra team will allow those.

Also please send the test API key TTL and any rate-limit headers we should include.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Integrations | FinWise
alex.johnson@finwise.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>, Chris Lee <chris@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs & next steps

Alex — moving the window to Sat 2027-07-03 00:00 - 02:00 UTC works for our side.

Answers to your bullets: 
- Streaming: we'll test true server push streaming (chunked responses). The k6 script includes a small client that opens a streaming session and measures time-to-first-chunk and inter-chunk latency — that mirrors your production clients.
- IP allowlist: confirmed — our infra team will add 52.23.112.45 and 35.182.90.12 to the test allowlist. We'll also add a temporary rule to limit access to the dedicated test route.
- Test API key: we'll provision a scoped test key valid for 48 hours (expires 2027-07-05T00:00:00Z). The key will be limited to the test endpoints and pre-populated test user IDs. Use the header Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>.

I've attached the finwise_k6_script.js and test_accounts.csv and a short load test plan PDF. Marissa — can you confirm the k6 ramp schedule and the token/header details to include?

Thanks — Logan

On a related note: hubspot deal FW-2027-0421 updated with the test window and plan: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs & next steps

Alex / team — attaching the k6 example and a short notes block here for the runners. Please use the included finwise_k6_script.js as the starting point. Key points: 

- Ramp profile: ramp to 500 VUs over 10m, hold for 90m, ramp down 10m. (Script uses stages: {duration: '10m', target: 500}, {duration: '90m', target: 500}, {duration: '10m', target: 0}).
- Concurrency: for streaming we simulate 200 concurrent streams by opening websocket-like connections using k6's http.batch with keep-alive; results include time-to-first-chunk and p95/p99 calculations.
- Headers & auth: set Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY> and x-redwood-test-user from test_accounts.csv. We also add x-request-id per request for tracing.
- Metrics: script emits custom metrics for chunk_latency_ms and tokens_per_second. We recommend collecting k6 output as Influx or CloudWatch for correlation with Redwood traces.

Test accounts: test_accounts.csv contains 500 rows (user_id,test_profile). Please rotate users across VUs to avoid hot-keying.

Let us know if you want a dry-run (low load) on Friday to validate connectivity.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
